question: What is the primary purpose of continuous cardiac monitoring in the clinical setting?

options.A: Replacing routine manual blood pressure checks

explanation: Continuous monitoring allows nurses to spot dangerous arrhythmias before they cause overt clinical deterioration. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T2#GNS212_U4_T2_h1)

question: A patient with chest pain is placed on a bedside cardiac monitor. Why is this observation vital?

options.A: It automatically administers emergency cardiac medications
options.B: It cures underlying coronary artery blockages
options.C: It eliminates the need for physical assessments
options.D: It gives immediate insight into sudden heart rate changes

explanation: Monitors provide real-time visual tracking of electrical activity, alerting staff to acute rhythm instability. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T2#GNS212_U4_T2_h1)

question: Which waveform on an ECG represents ventricular depolarization?
explanation: The QRS complex corresponds to the electrical activation and depolarization of the ventricles. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T2#GNS212_U4_T2_h2)

question: What physiological event does the P wave indicate on a cardiac monitor?
explanation: The P wave shows the spread of the electrical impulse across the atria. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T2#GNS212_U4_T2_h2)

question: Where should the white electrode be placed in a standard 3-lead monitoring setup?
explanation: Standard color coding places the white electrode on the right arm position. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T2#GNS212_U4_T2_h3)

question: A nurse notices a very weak and fuzzy ECG signal on a newly admitted patient. What action should be taken first?

options.A: Clean the skin and replace old electrode patches
options.B: Disconnect the patient from telemetry permanently
options.C: Replace the entire bedside monitoring machine

explanation: Skin oils and dry gel on old electrodes often cause poor signal transmission, which is easily fixed by proper skin prep and new patches. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T2#GNS212_U4_T2_h3)

question: Why should a nurse clip chest hair instead of shaving it before applying electrodes?

options.A: To prevent skin micro-abrasions and irritation
options.B: To make the adhesive stick permanently forever
options.C: To speed up hair growth after discharge
options.D: To prevent the monitor from shocking the patient

explanation: Shaving can cause tiny cuts that risk infection and increase skin sensitivity under the electrode gel. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T2#GNS212_U4_T2_h4)

question: How often should disposable cardiac electrodes typically be changed to maintain signal quality?

options.D: Only when the patient complains of itching

explanation: Electrode gel dries out and adhesive weakens over time, requiring daily replacement for optimal signal conduction. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T2#GNS212_U4_T2_h4)

question: What is the normal resting heart rate range for a healthy adult in sinus rhythm?
explanation: Normal sinus rhythm maintains a steady rate between 60 and 100 beats per minute in adults. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T2#GNS212_U4_T2_h5)

question: Which rhythm pattern on a cardiac monitor shows completely chaotic waves with no identifiable QRS complexes?
explanation: Ventricular fibrillation produces erratic, disorganized electrical activity without effective ventricular contractions. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T2#GNS212_U4_T2_h5)

question: A patient's monitor suddenly shows a flat line, but the patient is sitting up talking to visitors. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Check the lead connections and electrode contact
options.B: Immediately begin chest compressions and CPR
options.C: Silence the alarm and walk out of the room
options.D: Order an emergency serum electrolyte panel

explanation: A disconnected lead wire causes a flat line while the patient remains hemodynamically stable, so assessing equipment first prevents unnecessary panic. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T2#GNS212_U4_T2_h6)

question: What is the main cause of jagged baseline interference on a cardiac monitor screen?

options.A: A sudden drop in blood pressure

explanation: Somatic tremor from shivering or moving generates electrical noise that disrupts the baseline. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T2#GNS212_U4_T2_h6)

question: Why is physical assessment more important than relying only on the monitor screen?

options.A: Patients dislike looking at electronic display screens
options.B: Monitors can show artifacts while the patient has a stable pulse
options.C: Machines never experience electrical power failures
options.D: Doctors do not trust electronic heart rhythm data

explanation: Equipment errors or loose wires can mimic dangerous rhythms, making physical assessment necessary to confirm true distress. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T2#GNS212_U4_T2_h7)

question: What is an unsafe practice regarding monitor alarm management on a busy hospital ward?

options.A: Reporting broken alarm speakers to biomedical engineering
options.B: Responding promptly to high-priority visual warnings
options.C: Turning off alarm volumes permanently to reduce noise
options.D: Adjusting alarm limits to match the patient's baseline

explanation: Permanently disabling alarms puts patients at high risk because critical rhythm changes will go unnoticed. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T2#GNS212_U4_T2_h7)
